title: "Edge AI"
description: "The deployment or execution of AI workloads on devices near where data is collected or used."
term: "Edge AI"
letter: "E"
category: "AI Infrastructure"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Edge AI runs some or all AI processing on a local device or nearby
gateway instead of sending every input to a distant cloud service.
Examples include cameras, phones, vehicles, and industrial equipment.

## Technical explanation

Edge deployments operate under constraints such as limited compute,
memory, power, connectivity, and thermal capacity. Models may be
compressed, quantized, compiled, or specialized for available hardware.
A system can combine local inference with cloud-based training,
management, or fallback processing.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Local inference can reduce network latency, limit data transfer, and
support operation with intermittent connectivity. It also creates
challenges in model updates, device diversity, monitoring, security, and
resource budgeting.

## How it works

A trained model and its runtime are packaged for a target device.
Inputs are processed locally, and predictions or selected telemetry may
be sent to other systems. Deployment pipelines manage compatibility,
updates, observability, and fallback behaviour.

## Practical example

A camera can run a compact object detector locally to flag possible
equipment issues, sending only selected events to a central service
instead of streaming every frame.

## Common misconceptions

- Edge AI does not mean that a model never communicates with cloud
  services.
- Local processing does not automatically guarantee privacy or security.
- A model that runs on a developer's laptop may not meet the latency,
  power, or memory constraints of the target device.
